subject: SAC-B6e static residual scaling across heterogeneous fixtures
intent: Test whether the B6d static global-residual cap effect persists or reverses across fixtures with different feature-family cardinalities before considering adaptive policy.

fixtures.interpretation: text-dominant control reverses under proportional residual growth; both static caps restore desired ordering.
baseline already strongly preserves desired ordering. Static caps increase local distinct dimensions but slightly reduce the retrieval margin, so residual suppression is not uniformly beneficial.
higher text cardinality produces a stronger baseline reversal; both static caps recover positive ordering, with cap128 retaining a larger margin than cap64.

crossFixtureFindings: Static residual suppression recovered desired ordering in both text-dominant fixtures, but reduced the already-positive margin in the structure-heavy fixture.

cap128 produced a larger candidate margin than cap64 in all three evaluated fixtures, despite cap64 restoring more local incremental dimensions. More local-distinct dimensions are not a monotonic quality signal.

The two text-dominant fixtures share graph/provenance/grouping cardinalities and differ mainly in text feature count (61 versus 108); the baseline reversal becomes more negative as text cardinality rises in these synthetic examples.

The structure-heavy fixture has only 5 text features and 16 graph + 16 provenance features. Its proportional baseline remains strongest, showing that a static residual cap should not be treated as an unconditional improvement.

The result narrows the next research question from 'should residual be capped?' to 'under what workload/profile conditions should residual scaling be bounded?', while keeping input cardinality separate from semantic importance.

independentReconstruction.method: Independent deterministic reconstruction of byte-wise feature hashing, splitmix64 projection, SUI text n-grams and structured features, B1 family normalization, B2 local/global selection, signature union, containment, and cosine similarity.
independentReconstruction.result: reproduced all three fixture feature cardinalities, margins, and local incremental counts encoded in the Go regression fixture.
independentReconstruction.limitation: This is not an exact repository Go 1.25 execution.

stopLines: three synthetic fixtures != real workload generalization
cap128 beating cap64 here != globally optimal cap
text cardinality correlation != semantic importance rule
structure-heavy baseline advantage != universal no-cap rule
